propertyEvents.result: At June 30 margins the quarter’s jobs would have earned $2,180,047.50 of gross profit; they earned $1,797,327.50. One job explains it: Tideflats Cold Storage earned $82,800.00 on $4,048,000.00 of revenue, $382,720.00 below its June margin, because its estimate rose from $16,284,000.00 to $17,480,000.00 and the whole year-to-date effect lands in this quarter. propertyEvents.result: Test the change order the schedule counts before the owner has signed it
propertyEvents.locator: Sep 30 2026!A8:O16 and Jun 30 2026!A8:O15; contract, estimate, cost, earned revenue and billings by job

propertyEvents.result: Alder Point’s total contract includes pending change order PCO-14, $640,000.00, which the owner has not signed (Q2). At 40.5% complete it puts $259,200.00 into this quarter’s revenue and gross profit, more than materiality. Whether an unsigned change order can be counted yet is a judgment under the revenue standard’s limit on uncertain amounts; the CPA reads the pricing and the architect’s review (REV-01). Without it Alder Point would be $16,250.00 against its billings.

propertyEvents.result: Set an expectation for interest from each loan’s balance, rate and days, and compare it with the books
propertyEvents.locator: PDF page 1; term loan and line of credit activity, balances and the interest accrued for September

propertyEvents.result: From the balances, the rates and actual/360 days the quarter’s interest should be $98,140.50; the books show $91,455.50. The books’ figure is exactly what the bank debited on July 1, August 1 and September 1, the interest for June, July and August: interest is recorded when paid. September’s $35,350.00, on the bank’s own statement, is not accrued (accrued interest in the books: $0.00), and June’s $28,665.00 landed in this quarter. Expense is understated $6,685.00 and liabilities $35,350.00 (INT-01). This contradicts Q5, which says interest is accrued monthly (INQ-01).
propertyEvents.locator: PDF page 1; term loan and line of credit activity, balances and the interest accrued for September

propertyEvents.result: Recompute the three loan covenants as the agreement defines them
propertyEvents.locator: PDF page 1; section 7 financial covenants, interest terms and definitions

propertyEvents.result: Working capital $4,789,499.00 (minimum $3,000,000) and total liabilities to tangible net worth 2.46 to 1 (maximum 2.75) are met. Tangible net worth must leave out everything due from affiliates: Juniper Row’s $571,000.00 receivable, $94,000.00 retainage and $50,500.00 underbilled, $715,500.00 in all. That leaves $6,629,999.00, $129,999.00 above the $6,500,000 minimum. Record INT-01 and leave out PCO-14 and it falls to $6,335,449.00, $164,551.00 short: the covenant, and whether the loans stay long-term, turn on the CPA’s judgment on PCO-14 (COV-01).

propertyEvents.result: Wages tie to payroll · interest recorded when paid, $35,350 not accrued · covenants met with $129,999 of net worth headroom
Ready for the CPA
Add up what was found and set it against materiality

Known misstatements add up to $6,685.00 of expense, 6.7% of the $100,000.00 materiality, with $35,350.00 of accrued interest missing from liabilities (INT-01). The judgment that matters is larger: PCO-14 puts $259,200.00 into revenue before the owner has signed, 259% of materiality, and decides the net worth covenant (REV-01, COV-01). The statements also need a related party note for Juniper Row (RP-01). Concluding is the CPA’s job; the machine stops here.

log.text: From the balances, the rates and actual/360 days the quarter’s interest should be $98,140.50; the books show $91,455.50. The books’ figure is exactly what the bank debited on July 1, August 1 and September 1, the interest for June, July and August: interest is recorded when paid. September’s $35,350.00, on the bank’s own statement, is not accrued (accrued interest in the books: $0.00), and June’s $28,665.00 landed in this quarter. Expense is understated $6,685.00 and liabilities $35,350.00 (INT-01). This contradicts Q5, which says interest is accrued monthly (INQ-01).

log.text: Working capital $4,789,499.00 (minimum $3,000,000) and total liabilities to tangible net worth 2.46 to 1 (maximum 2.75) are met. Tangible net worth must leave out everything due from affiliates: Juniper Row’s $571,000.00 receivable, $94,000.00 retainage and $50,500.00 underbilled, $715,500.00 in all. That leaves $6,629,999.00, $129,999.00 above the $6,500,000 minimum. Record INT-01 and leave out PCO-14 and it falls to $6,335,449.00, $164,551.00 short: the covenant, and whether the loans stay long-term, turn on the CPA’s judgment on PCO-14 (COV-01).

The judgment that matters is larger: PCO-14 puts $259,200.00 into revenue before the owner has signed, 259% of materiality, and decides the net worth covenant (REV-01, COV-01).
